questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had never been to Paris before, and I was very curious to try and live there. I also heard good things about the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to make contact with the university, and the website is confusing to navigate.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received assistance from responsables of exchange/mobility of the university. It was however still difficult to clarify questions and issues.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy since I applied through Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris and got a spot shortly after I applied.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I will highly recommend CIUP. Very nice place with a lot of other international students. Affordable prices.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A long time went by without knowing anything about the registration process, and when it finally came, we had very little time to choose. But it worked fine as soon as I was able to apply.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was assistance, but I would not always get replies.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was succesful, I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of how many English courses they offer, as they inform that it is possible to do only English courses, but it is not guaranteed that you can get English courses worth 30 ECTS.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses varied significantly. Though the courses were very small (4 ECTS), the amount of stuff you had to learn was big in some of the courses. But the overall level was appropriate, I will say.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is very different. No books to study, only relying on powerpoints which sometimes had very little info.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
European International Relations
International Investment Law
Law and Economics
Philosophy of Law
European Law
History and Principles of French Intellectual Property Law
History of the European Legal System
I also had a compulsory French language class

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
European International Relations - very interesting
International Investment Law - very interesting and high level
Law and Economics - very interesting for a law student, because you get a different approach (economic approach)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was very expensive to do laundry which was unexpected. Other than that nothing really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Bakeries, groceries, restaurants had fair prices, a little less expensive than DK.
Public transport was a lot more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Activities such as wine and cheese tastings and trip to the Senate

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Versailles, go to the parks and chill in the weekends, see museums, walk along the Seine. Just explore the streets of Paris.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A bit difficult because I didn't speak much French.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speaking French to some level is a big advantage. The students were very nice, but a bit longer.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Again, that they are not used to speaking English to the same extent as Danish people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very kind people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The administrative process can be a bit challenging, but it is not too unusual when going on exchange, I heard. 
It's a very big advantage to speak some French.
I will recommend to look for accommodation at CIUP.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Paris is an amazing city to live in overall.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural exchange, the people you meet and also what you learn at university and about yourself on the journey.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning to speak French and be friends with the locals.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
